_about: Legend: The Kelpie (Loch Sunart), lines for H1+E1 (Jonny picked 27 Nov 23:34 Berlin). Speakers: N narrator, G grandmother, K kid, A village kid. Frame 0 = kelpie kneeling in the loch; last shot = Grandma's nine-finger hand on L28.

G.style: an old woman in her eighties, warm but stern, low slightly raspy voice, slow and calm

K.style: a twelve-year-old boy from a film, natural child actor, clearly a boy, voice not broken yet, curious and quietly worried, speaks clearly with crisp diction
K._af: ep1 kid EQ, applied up front (wolf video: 7 of its kid takes read MUFFLED)

A.style: a cheeky eleven-year-old village boy, loud, natural child actor

lines: If a horse kneels for you by the loch, never touch it.
Loch Sunart, Scotland. Eleven at night. Three kids from the village found it waiting in the water.
cheeky, excited, shouting across the water
It knelt. The first one climbed on. Then the second. Then the third.
And its back grew longer with every child.
Never touch it. And if you ever do, find the bridle.
But the horse turned its wet face to him. And waited.
In Scotland they call it the kelpie, and every loch has one.
I can't get off! My hands won't let go!
Then the kelpie turned, and walked into the loch.
Water to his knees. To his chest. The kids on its back screamed.
Under the mane, his free hand found something. Cold. Braided. Little silver rings.
The kelpie froze. Then it knelt, in the water. For him.
The kids slid off. His finger came loose.
I didn't touch it. I own it.
